title: Was Santa Claus Real? The Bishop Whose Bones Were Stolen
hook: Santa Claus grew out of a real man, and sailors once broke into his tomb and carried off his bones.
era: Roman Empire, the city of Myra in what is now Turkey, about 330 AD
thumbnail_picture: Big and close on the right: a cracked-open stone tomb in a torch-lit church with pale bones glowing inside, and a wide-eyed medieval sailor in a rough tunic gasping at it, shocked face, deep shadows, left third empty.
description:
Was Santa Claus a real man? Meet Saint Nicholas of Myra, the secret-gift bishop from what is now Turkey whose bones were stolen by sailors, and see how a Dutch Sinterklaas became Santa Claus.

The true story of Santa Claus: a 4th-century Greek-speaking Roman bishop, a daring theft in 1087, and how his legend ended up at the North Pole. Legends are told as legends.

Sources and further reading:
- Charles W. Jones, Saint Nicholas of Myra, Bari, and Manhattan: Biography of a Legend (University of Chicago Press)
- Gerry Bowler, Santa Claus: A Biography
- Adam English, The Saint Who Would Be Santa Claus
- Basilica di San Nicola, Bari (records of the 1087 translation of the relics)
tags: where did santa claus come from

scenes.narration: Santa Claus grew out of a real man, and sailors once smashed into his tomb and stole his bones.
scenes.delivery: hushed, urgent, a hint of disbelief
scenes.caption: THE REAL SANTA
scenes.era: Myra in what is now Turkey, 1087 AD
scenes.picture: Three rough bearded medieval sailors in tunics and leather belts prying open a cracked marble tomb with iron bars inside a dark stone church at night, torchlight flickering, pale bones visible inside, tense faces, Myra, 1087 AD.

scenes.narration: Some of those stolen bones still lie in a church in Italy today, and pilgrims still climb its steps.
scenes.caption: STILL IN ITALY
scenes.picture: Grand Romanesque stone basilica with two square towers beside the blue sea at sunrise, a few pilgrims in long cloaks climbing wide stone steps toward its arched doorway, Bari, Italy, about 1100 AD, calm peaceful mood.

scenes.narration: So how does a Greek-speaking bishop from what is now Turkey end up as a jolly man at the North Pole?
scenes.caption: THE BIG QUESTION
scenes.picture: Wide shot of a cheerful cartoon Santa Claus with a white beard and red suit laughing in a flying sleigh pulled by reindeer high above a snowy night village with glowing windows and a big moon.

scenes.narration: Let's test the story everyone knows, one claim at a time. Some of it is nonsense. Some of it is stranger than you'd guess.
scenes.caption: MYTH CHECK
scenes.picture: Small child in pajamas peeking wide-eyed around a doorway corner at a glowing decorated Christmas tree and a red stocking hanging by a fireplace, cozy living room at night, curious smile.

scenes.narration: First claim: Santa lives at the North Pole, with elves and flying reindeer.
scenes.caption: CLAIM: NORTH POLE
scenes.picture: Snowy wooden toy workshop at the North Pole with glowing yellow windows, three small cartoon elves in pointed hats carrying toys across the snow, reindeer waiting outside beside a sleigh, starry sky.

scenes.narration: Nope. The real man lived on a warm Mediterranean coast, nowhere near the Arctic. Tradition says he was born in Patara around 270.
scenes.caption: PATARA, ABOUT 270
scenes.picture: Small boy in a simple linen tunic standing on a sunny stone quay watching fishing boats, white stone Roman houses and palm trees behind him, warm blue Mediterranean coast, Patara, Roman Lycia, about 270 AD.

scenes.narration: Years later he became bishop of Myra, a Roman city whose busy harbor, Andriake, lay just down the coast.
scenes.caption: MYRA
scenes.picture: Wide view of the busy Roman harbor of Andriake: tall wooden cargo ships moored at a stone quay, large grain warehouses with arched doors, green hills rising behind, bright daylight, Roman Empire, about 330 AD.

scenes.narration: Historians think Myra sat on the sea road carrying Egypt's wheat toward Rome, so sailors passed through all the time.
scenes.caption: A SAILORS' TOWN
scenes.picture: Roman dockworkers in short tunics hauling heavy grain sacks down a ship's wooden plank onto a stone quay, a sailor shouting orders, sunny day, loaded cargo ship behind them, Roman Empire.

scenes.narration: Now here's the twist. The famous gift-giving story is one of the oldest tales about him, and it's a legend.
scenes.caption: LEGEND, NOT RECORD
scenes.picture: Nicholas, a lean middle-aged bishop with a short grey beard and kind eyes in a plain cream wool robe, walking alone down a quiet moonlit cobbled street of a Roman town, holding a small cloth sack.

scenes.narration: The tale goes like this. A poor man in Myra had three daughters and no money for their marriages.
scenes.caption: THE POOR FATHER
scenes.picture: Worried poor Roman father with thinning dark hair and a ragged tunic sitting at a rough wooden table, three young women in simple tunics standing close beside him, dim oil lamp glowing, bare stone room.

scenes.narration: No dowry meant no weddings, and maybe a much worse future. He was out of options.
scenes.caption: NO MONEY
scenes.picture: Close-up of an empty leather coin purse turned upside down on a rough wooden table, a poor father's weathered hands pressed against his forehead above it, dim lamplight, despair.

scenes.narration: So Nicholas crept up at night, the story says, and tossed a bag of gold through the window.
scenes.caption: A SECRET GIFT
scenes.picture: Night scene: Nicholas, a lean middle-aged bishop with a short grey beard and kind eyes in a plain cream wool robe, tossing a small pouch of gold coins through a small open window of a stone house, moonlight.

scenes.narration: He did it again, then a third time. But on the last night, the father stayed up and caught him.
scenes.caption: CAUGHT
scenes.picture: Dawn at a stone doorway: a startled poor father with thinning dark hair gripping the sleeve of Nicholas, a lean middle-aged bishop with a short grey beard in a plain cream wool robe, who is turning to flee, soft pink light.

scenes.narration: Nicholas begged him to keep quiet. He didn't want credit. He wanted it secret.
scenes.caption: NO CREDIT
scenes.picture: Close-up of Nicholas, a lean middle-aged bishop with a short grey beard and kind eyes in a plain cream wool robe, holding a finger to his lips with pleading eyes, a grateful tearful father blurred behind him.

scenes.narration: Careful, though. Monks wrote that down hundreds of years after he died, so treat it as a legend.
scenes.caption: WRITTEN LATER
scenes.picture: Monk in a brown hooded robe copying a long story with a quill on parchment at a wooden desk in a candle-lit stone monastery room, shelves of scrolls behind him, quiet and serious, Byzantine Empire, about 850 AD.

scenes.narration: And the stocking by the fireplace? Later folk versions had socks drying by the fire, with the gold landing inside. Nobody knows exactly when that crept in.
scenes.caption: THE STOCKING
scenes.picture: Close-up of gold coins tumbling from above into a hanging woolen sock beside a small stone hearth, glowing orange firelight, simple Roman-style room, warm cozy mood.

scenes.narration: So what do we actually know about the man? Less than you'd hope.
scenes.caption: WHAT'S SOLID
scenes.picture: Old stone church standing alone on a quiet Mediterranean hillside at dawn, mist filling the valley below, olive trees, soft golden light, calm and mysterious, Roman Empire, 300s AD.

scenes.narration: He was very likely a real bishop of Myra in the 300s. Tradition says he died on December 6, around 343, and people kept his tomb.
scenes.caption: TRADITION: ABOUT 343
scenes.picture: Inside an early Christian stone church, a simple marble tomb in the center, three villagers in plain tunics lighting small oil lamps around it, soft warm glow, quiet respectful mood.

scenes.narration: Everything else, the storms, the rescued prisoners, the miracles, piled up later, one retelling at a time.
scenes.caption: THE LEGEND GROWS
scenes.picture: Villagers gathered around a night campfire on a hillside in a Roman-era town, an old man in a plain tunic telling a story with wide arm gestures, a few captivated listeners, sparks rising into the dark sky.

scenes.narration: Take the storm story. Sailors in trouble prayed to him, and the waves supposedly calmed.
scenes.caption: STORM LEGEND
scenes.picture: Wooden Roman sailing ship tossed by huge dark waves in a storm, terrified sailors clinging to the mast, torn sail, a break of golden light opening in the clouds above.

scenes.narration: That's why sailors made him their patron saint. Remember that, because sailors are about to commit a crime.
scenes.caption: PATRON OF SAILORS
scenes.picture: Three sailors in tunics kneeling in prayer at a small harbor shrine with a lit oil lamp at dusk, wooden ships moored behind them, calm orange sky, Roman port.

scenes.narration: Another claim: he slapped a rival at the great Council of Nicaea in 325. But it's a late legend, and Nicholas isn't on the surviving lists of who attended.
scenes.caption: NICAEA, 325
scenes.picture: Grand hall full of robed bishops seated in rows, one bishop with a white beard raising his hand in anger while another recoils in shock, columns and arches, Council of Nicaea, Roman Empire, 325 AD.

scenes.narration: Verdict: almost certainly invented. But it shows how fast a good legend grows.
scenes.caption: VERDICT: MYTH
scenes.picture: Roman market square with townspeople in tunics whispering to each other and pointing, one grinning man leaning in to spread a tale, stalls with fruit and pottery behind, sunny day.

scenes.narration: Meanwhile his tomb in Myra became a pilgrim magnet, and visitors kept coming for about seven hundred years.
scenes.caption: A PILGRIM MAGNET
scenes.picture: Long line of medieval pilgrims with walking staffs and small clay jars climbing a stony path toward a stone church on a sunny hillside, travel-worn cloaks, Myra, Byzantine Empire, about 900 AD.

scenes.narration: Legend said a clear, sweet liquid seeped from his bones, so pilgrims carried it home in tiny bottles.
scenes.caption: THE HOLY LIQUID
scenes.picture: Close-up of hands holding a small glass flask of clear liquid beside a carved stone tomb, candle glow reflecting in the glass, Myra church, Byzantine Empire, about 900 AD.

scenes.narration: Then trouble arrived. In 1071 the Seljuk Turks crushed a Byzantine army, and the whole region felt unsafe.
scenes.picture: Seljuk horsemen in turbans and lamellar armor on a dusty ridge looking down over a plain full of retreating Byzantine soldiers, red sunset sky, banners-free battlefield, Anatolia, 1071 AD.

scenes.narration: Across the sea, the Italian port of Bari had lost its Byzantine rulers to the Normans that same year, and it badly wanted a famous saint of its own.
scenes.caption: BARI WANTS A SAINT
scenes.picture: Bustling medieval Italian port with merchants in tunics bargaining on a stone quay, small ships at anchor, two men whispering and glancing at the sea with scheming looks, Bari, Italy, 1087 AD.

scenes.narration: Their plan was simple: sail to Myra as merchants, scout the church, and say they only wanted to pray there.
scenes.caption: THE PLAN
scenes.picture: Three small medieval merchant ships with square sails crossing a bright blue sea, bearded sailors on deck looking ahead toward the horizon, white clouds, Mediterranean Sea, 1087 AD.

scenes.narration: In April 1087, according to the Bari accounts, about forty-seven men from Bari came ashore and headed up to the church.
scenes.caption: APRIL 1087
scenes.era: Myra in what is now Turkey, 1087 AD
scenes.picture: Group of rough bearded medieval sailors in tunics and leather belts leaving a small harbor quay and walking up a dirt road toward a distant hillside stone church, wary expressions, Myra, 1087 AD.

scenes.narration: Four monks guarded the tomb. The sailors offered gold. The monks said no.
scenes.caption: THE MONKS SAY NO
scenes.era: Myra in what is now Turkey, 1087 AD
scenes.picture: Four monks in plain dark robes standing with arms crossed in front of a marble tomb inside a stone church while a bearded sailor holds out a heavy purse of coins, monks shaking their heads, Myra, 1087 AD.

scenes.narration: So the sailors tried something less polite. According to the Bari account, they smashed the tomb open.
scenes.caption: BREAKING IN
scenes.era: Myra in what is now Turkey, 1087 AD
scenes.picture: Bearded medieval sailor in a tunic swinging an iron hammer at a marble tomb slab, sparks flying, torchlight flickering, two other sailors watching nervously, dark stone church, Myra, 1087 AD.

scenes.narration: Inside, the story goes, the bones lay in that sweet-smelling liquid.
scenes.caption: THE BONES
scenes.era: Myra in what is now Turkey, 1087 AD
scenes.picture: Close-up inside an open stone tomb, pale bones glistening in clear liquid, lit by a single torch from the side, dark shadows, Myra, 1087 AD.

scenes.narration: They wrapped the bones up and hurried to the ships. By then word had spread, and locals followed them down to the shore, looking on in dismay.
scenes.caption: THE GETAWAY
scenes.era: Myra in what is now Turkey, 1087 AD
scenes.picture: Bearded sailors in tunics hurrying down a stone harbor quay carrying a heavy wooden chest between them, a ship waiting, blurred alarmed townspeople watching from behind in dismay, Myra, 1087 AD.

scenes.narration: Did they call it theft? Of course not. They called it a rescue.
scenes.caption: A 'RESCUE'
scenes.picture: Smug bearded sailors lounging casually on a medieval ship's deck around a wooden chest covered with a cloth, sea spray, bright sky, one sailor winking, Mediterranean Sea, 1087 AD.

scenes.narration: In early May 1087, Bari welcomed the ship home, and the city still celebrates the day on May 9.
scenes.caption: BARI, MAY 8–9
scenes.picture: Huge cheering crowd on a harbor quay waving as a medieval ship with a square sail arrives, colorful cloth pennants, bright morning light, joyful faces, Bari, Italy, 1087 AD.

scenes.narration: Today a huge church holds the bones in its crypt, and pilgrims still line up to see them.
scenes.caption: THE CRYPT
scenes.picture: Candle-lit stone crypt with a plain stone altar, a row of pilgrims kneeling quietly with bowed heads, soft golden light, round arches, Bari, Italy, today.

scenes.narration: But Venice grumbled. In 1099 and 1100, Venetian crusaders stopped at Myra too, and took what they said were the pieces Bari had missed.
scenes.caption: VENICE 1099–1100
scenes.era: Myra in what is now Turkey, 1099–1100 AD
scenes.picture: Venetian galleys with oars anchored near a rocky coast, armored crusaders in a small rowboat heading to shore at dusk, orange sky, Myra, 1099 AD.

scenes.narration: Yes, two cities claim the same saint. In the 1950s an anatomist examined the Bari bones. Later work suggests the Venice fragments fit the same skeleton. That doesn't prove whose skeleton it is.
scenes.caption: SCIENCE STEPS IN
scenes.picture: Scientist in a white coat in a plain 1950s laboratory carefully studying old pale bones laid out on a table, magnifying glass in hand, a bare lamp overhead, Italy.

scenes.narration: Turkey hasn't forgotten, though. In 2017, scans revealed unexcavated spaces beneath the old church in Demre.
scenes.caption: HIDDEN SPACES
scenes.picture: Two archaeologists in modern work clothes pushing a ground-penetrating radar cart across the stone floor of an old Byzantine church, one checking a handheld device, Demre, Turkey, 2017.

scenes.narration: Some hope those spaces hold something the sailors missed. Nobody knows yet, so the mystery stays open.
scenes.caption: UNSOLVED
scenes.picture: Old Byzantine stone church in Demre at golden hour, a lone visitor looking up at its arches, long warm shadows, quiet and hopeful, Turkey, today.

scenes.narration: Fine, but how does a bishop become Santa? That's where the Dutch come in.
scenes.caption: ENTER THE DUTCH
scenes.picture: Narrow Dutch canal street in winter with tall brick gabled houses, snow on the roofs, townspeople in wool coats and hats walking along the frozen canal, Netherlands, 1500s.

scenes.narration: By the late Middle Ages, December 6 was Saint Nicholas Day, and in many places children left their shoes out, hoping the saint would fill them.
scenes.caption: DECEMBER 6
scenes.picture: Two children in wool clothes placing wooden shoes beside a brick hearth in a cozy room with a flickering fire, excited faces, Netherlands, 1500s.

scenes.narration: Then the Reformation came, and many Protestants cancelled their saints, gift-givers included. Nicholas was in danger of vanishing.
scenes.caption: SAINTS CANCELLED
scenes.picture: Workers in plain clothes whitewashing the painted walls inside a stone church, saint statues stacked on the floor, two stern onlookers in dark Protestant clothes, Northern Europe, 1500s.

scenes.narration: But the Dutch just refused to let go. Sinterklaas stayed: a tall bishop in red, with a pointed hat and a white horse.
scenes.caption: SINTERKLAAS
scenes.picture: Sinterklaas, a tall bishop with a long white beard in a red robe and pointed red hat, riding a white horse down a snowy Dutch street at dusk while delighted children watch, Netherlands, 1800s.

scenes.narration: Kids left a shoe by the chimney, with a carrot for the horse. By morning, there were sweets.
scenes.caption: SHOE AND CARROT
scenes.picture: Close-up of a wooden shoe holding a carrot beside a brick fireplace, a few wrapped sweets next to it, soft morning light, Netherlands, 1800s.

scenes.narration: Dutch settlers also sailed to New Amsterdam in the 1600s. Did they bring Sinterklaas along? Many historians doubt it.
scenes.caption: NEW AMSTERDAM
scenes.picture: Dutch merchant ship anchored off a tiny wooden settlement with a windmill and small wooden houses, settlers in wool coats rowing ashore with crates, New Amsterdam, 1640s.

scenes.narration: What we do know: by 1809, New Yorkers like writer Washington Irving were joking about a Dutch Saint Nicholas.
scenes.caption: NEW YORK, 1809
scenes.picture: Smiling writer in an early 1800s dark coat writing with a quill at a candle-lit desk, a small carved wooden figure of a pipe-smoking old man on the desk, New York, 1809.

scenes.narration: Then in 1823 a poem gave him a sleigh, eight reindeer, and a trip down the chimney. Who wrote it? People still argue.
scenes.caption: THE 1823 POEM
scenes.picture: Small round cheerful old man with a white beard and a pipe on a snowy rooftop beside a tiny sleigh pulled by eight tiny reindeer under a full moon, early 1800s storybook style, New York, 1823.

scenes.narration: The poem called him a 'jolly old elf' with a miniature sleigh. It took a cartoonist to make him big.
scenes.caption: MAKING HIM BIG
scenes.picture: Cartoonist in a vest at a slanted drawing desk sketching a large bearded man in fur-trimmed clothes with a pen, ink pots and loose papers around him, New York, 1860s.

scenes.narration: From 1863, Thomas Nast popularized a round, bearded Santa, and by the late 1860s he was busy in a toy workshop at the North Pole.
scenes.caption: THOMAS NAST
scenes.picture: Jolly round bearded man in a fur-trimmed suit carving a wooden toy at a workbench in a log cabin, finished toys on shelves, snow outside the window, 1800s style.

scenes.narration: Why the North Pole? One likely reason: nobody had been there to disprove it. No neighbors to complain.
scenes.caption: WHY THE POLE?
scenes.picture: Vast empty snowfield under a pale sky with one tiny cabin glowing warmly in the distance, a single path of footprints leading to it, silent and remote, Arctic.

scenes.narration: And the red suit? Coca-Cola didn't invent it. Santa was already wearing red long before the ads of the 1930s.
scenes.caption: RED SUIT MYTH
scenes.picture: Commercial artist in a 1930s studio painting a smiling grandfatherly Santa in a red suit on a big canvas, brushes and paint jars around him, United States, 1930s.

scenes.narration: Meanwhile the name drifted. English speakers said Sinterklaas fast, and it turned into Santa Claus.
scenes.caption: A SQUASHED NAME
scenes.picture: Dutch and English neighbors in old-fashioned 1700s clothes chatting over a market stall, one man cupping his ear and laughing, baskets of apples, old New York.

scenes.narration: So here's the real chain. A quiet bishop on a warm coast in what is now Turkey, giving in secret, became the saint of sailors.
scenes.caption: THE CHAIN
scenes.picture: Nicholas, a lean middle-aged bishop with a short grey beard and kind eyes in a plain cream wool robe, walking alone along a moonlit Roman harbor carrying a small sack, ships quiet beside him.

scenes.narration: Then sailors stole his bones, and the theft turbocharged his cult in western Europe.
scenes.caption: ACROSS THE SEA
scenes.picture: Medieval ship with a square sail crossing a calm sea at sunset, golden light on the water, sailors silhouetted on deck, Mediterranean Sea, 1087 AD.

scenes.narration: The Dutch kept him alive when others dropped him, and New Yorkers turned him into a laughing man in a sleigh.
scenes.caption: KEPT ALIVE
scenes.picture: Dutch family at a snowy evening window, a child pointing excitedly at a distant red-robed bishop on a white horse passing in the street, warm lamplight inside, Netherlands, 1800s.

scenes.narration: The funniest part? The real Nicholas wanted no credit. His whole thing was giving in secret.
scenes.caption: THE IRONY
scenes.picture: Night scene of Nicholas, a lean middle-aged bishop with a short grey beard and kind eyes in a plain cream wool robe, slipping a small bag through a dark window of a stone house, faint smile, moonlight on his face.

scenes.narration: Now children in most of the world know his name, even if they say it wrong.
scenes.caption: FAMOUS ANYWAY
scenes.picture: Excited children in pajamas tearing open gifts around a Christmas tree on a bright winter morning, parents laughing on a sofa, wrapping paper everywhere, today.

scenes.narration: So was Santa real? Not the guy with the reindeer. But the generous bishop? Very likely real, and he lived in what is now Turkey.
scenes.caption: THE VERDICT
scenes.picture: Bronze statue of a kindly bishop with a sack of gifts in a sunny small-town square in Turkey, a few children standing around it looking up, Demre, today.

scenes.narration: Every December you repeat the name of a bishop from the Turkish coast, squashed into a Dutch word and wrapped in a poem.
scenes.caption: HIS NAME, SQUASHED
scenes.picture: Close-up of a hand placing a wrapped gift with a ribbon under a decorated Christmas tree, warm twinkling lights glowing, cozy evening, today.

scenes.narration: The North Pole is just where we parked him. His real home was a warm Mediterranean coast, in what is now Turkey.
scenes.caption: HOME: MYRA
scenes.picture: Quiet Roman harbor at sunset with a single small lamp glowing in a church window on the hill, calm water, Nicholas, a lean middle-aged bishop with a short grey beard in a plain cream wool robe, walking down to the shore.

narrator: Witty, confident myth-buster, a little sarcastic, quick, punchy, delighted by the truth.

short.title: Was Santa Real? Sailors Stole His Bones
short.description:
In 1087, sailors broke into a tomb in Turkey and stole the bones of the bishop behind Santa Claus. So was Santa real?
The true story of Saint Nicholas, the Bari theft and how he became Santa.

scenes.narration: In 1087, sailors stole the bones of the man behind Santa Claus, so was Santa real?
scenes.caption: TURKEY, 1087
scenes.era: Myra in what is now Turkey, 1087 AD
scenes.picture: Three rough medieval Italian sailors in coarse brown tunics lift pale bones out of a cracked marble tomb inside a dim stone church at night, torchlight flickering, tense sweating faces, dramatic shadows.

scenes.narration: Why steal bones from a Turkish tomb?
scenes.caption: WAS SANTA REAL?
scenes.picture: Cartoon Santa Claus in a red suit and white beard, one eyebrow raised, puzzled face, scratching his chin beside an ancient cracked marble tomb in a dim stone church, snowy window behind him.

scenes.narration: The man was Nicholas, a bishop of the Roman town of Myra.
scenes.caption: BISHOP NICHOLAS
scenes.picture: Saint Nicholas, a kindly elderly bishop with a short grey beard, tan skin and a plain brown wool robe with a simple cross, standing on a sunny stone quay of the Roman harbor town of Myra, blue sea and white stone buildings behind.

scenes.narration: Legend says Nicholas secretly gave gold to the poor.
scenes.caption: SECRET GIFTS
scenes.picture: Saint Nicholas, a kindly elderly bishop with a short grey beard and a plain brown wool robe, tossing a small pouch of gold coins through a tiny window of a poor stone house at night, moonlight on his face.

scenes.narration: But the Italian port of Bari wanted a famous saint.
scenes.caption: BARI WANTS A SAINT
scenes.picture: Two scheming medieval Italian merchants in dark velvet caps and long tunics whispering close together on a stone quay of the port of Bari, sly faces in the foreground, wooden ships blurred behind.

scenes.narration: So in 1087, about forty-seven Bari men sailed to Myra.
scenes.caption: THE VOYAGE
scenes.picture: A medieval wooden merchant ship with one big square sail cutting through bright blue Mediterranean waves, a few rough sailors in coarse tunics on deck looking ahead, the ship large and filling the frame.

scenes.narration: They said they only wanted to pray.
scenes.caption: A FAKE PLAN
scenes.era: Myra in what is now Turkey, 1087 AD
scenes.picture: Two rough medieval Italian sailors in coarse brown tunics with folded hands and fake innocent smiles standing at the arched wooden door of a stone church in Myra, wary sideways eyes.

scenes.narration: But four monks guarded the tomb, refusing their gold.
scenes.caption: MONKS SAY NO
scenes.era: Myra in what is now Turkey, 1087 AD
scenes.picture: Four monks in dark hooded robes with arms crossed, blocking a white marble tomb in a stone church, while one rough medieval Italian sailor in a coarse brown tunic holds out a heavy purse of gold coins.

scenes.narration: So they smashed the tomb open and took the bones.
scenes.caption: BREAKING IN
scenes.era: Myra in what is now Turkey, 1087 AD
scenes.picture: A rough medieval Italian sailor in a coarse brown tunic swings an iron hammer down onto a white marble tomb slab, sparks and stone chips flying, torchlight flickering in the dark church.

scenes.narration: They sailed home to Bari, where a huge church still holds them.
scenes.caption: BARI TODAY
scenes.picture: A medieval wooden ship with a square sail glides into the stone harbor of Bari at sunrise, rough sailors on deck holding up a small wooden chest, joyful faces, a blurred crowd waving on the quay.

scenes.narration: The Dutch kept honoring Nicholas as Sinterklaas, and New Yorkers turned him into Santa Claus.
scenes.caption: SINTERKLAAS TO SANTA
scenes.picture: Sinterklaas, a tall old bishop with a long white beard, a red robe and a tall pointed red hat, riding a white horse down a snowy Dutch brick street at dusk, two wide-eyed children watching from a doorway.

scenes.narration: So Santa with reindeer wasn't real, but bishop Nicholas very likely was.
scenes.caption: THE ANSWER
scenes.picture: A bronze statue of a kindly bishop with a short beard holding a sack of gifts, standing in a sunny small-town square in Demre, Turkey, with three smiling children looking up at it, palm trees and blue sky.
